Question 1 of 20, Level 1

1MCQCBSE 20241 mark
Direction ratios of a vector parallel to the line x−12=−y=2z+16\dfrac{x-1}{2} = -y = \dfrac{2z+1}{6}2x−1​=−y=62z+1​ are:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea In x−x1a=y−y1b=z−z1c\dfrac{x-x_1}{a} = \dfrac{y-y_1}{b} = \dfrac{z-z_1}{c}ax−x1​​=by−y1​​=cz−z1​​ the coefficients of x,y,zx, y, zx,y,z are 111; DRs are a,b,ca, b, ca,b,c.

  1. 1

    Write −y-y−y as y−1\dfrac{y}{-1}−1y​.

    −y=y−0−1-y = \dfrac{y-0}{-1}−y=−1y−0​
  2. 2

    Divide top and bottom of the last fraction by 222.

    2z+16=z+123\dfrac{2z+1}{6} = \dfrac{z+\frac{1}{2}}{3}62z+1​=3z+21​​2z+16=z+123\displaystyle \dfrac{2z+1}{6} = \dfrac{z+\frac{1}{2}}{3}62z+1​=3z+21​​
  3. 3

    Write the line in standard form.

    x−12=y−0−1=z+123\dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y-0}{-1} = \dfrac{z+\frac{1}{2}}{3}2x−1​=−1y−0​=3z+21​​x−12=y−0−1=z+123\displaystyle \dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y-0}{-1} = \dfrac{z+\frac{1}{2}}{3}2x−1​=−1y−0​=3z+21​​
  4. 4

    Read the denominators as direction ratios.

    DRs=2, −1, 3\text{DRs} = 2,\ -1,\ 3DRs=2, −1, 3
    1
  5. 5

    Hence the answer is option (D).

Answer(D) 2,−1,3\displaystyle 2, -1, 32,−1,3

Watch out Reading 666 from 2z+16\dfrac{2z+1}{6}62z+1​ (option A) without first making the coefficient of zzz equal to 111.

2MCQCBSE 20241 mark
If a line makes an angle of 30∘30^\circ30∘ with the positive direction of xxx-axis, 120∘120^\circ120∘ with the positive direction of yyy-axis, then the angle which it makes with the positive direction of zzz-axis is:

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea If a line makes angles α,β,γ\alpha, \beta, \gammaα,β,γ with the axes, then cos⁡2α+cos⁡2β+cos⁡2γ=1\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ=1.

  1. 1

    Use the identity for direction cosines.

    cos⁡230∘+cos⁡2120∘+cos⁡2γ=1\cos^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 120^\circ + \cos^2\gamma = 1cos230∘+cos2120∘+cos2γ=1cos⁡230∘+cos⁡2120∘+cos⁡2γ=1\displaystyle \cos^2 30^\circ + \cos^2 120^\circ + \cos^2\gamma = 1cos230∘+cos2120∘+cos2γ=1
  2. 2

    Put the values of the cosines.

    (32)2+(−12)2+cos⁡2γ=1\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \cos^2\gamma = 1(23​​)2+(−21​)2+cos2γ=1(32)2+(−12)2+cos⁡2γ=1\displaystyle \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 + \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + \cos^2\gamma = 1(23​​)2+(−21​)2+cos2γ=1
  3. 3

    Simplify.

    34+14+cos⁡2γ=1  ⇒  cos⁡2γ=0\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \cos^2\gamma = 043​+41​+cos2γ=1⇒cos2γ=034+14+cos⁡2γ=1  ⇒  cos⁡2γ=0\displaystyle \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \cos^2\gamma = 1 \;\Rightarrow\; \cos^2\gamma = 043​+41​+cos2γ=1⇒cos2γ=0
  4. 4

    Solve for γ\gammaγ.

    cos⁡γ=0  ⇒  γ=90∘\cos\gamma = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \gamma = 90^\circcosγ=0⇒γ=90∘cos⁡γ=0  ⇒  γ=90∘\displaystyle \cos\gamma = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \gamma = 90^\circcosγ=0⇒γ=90∘
    1
  5. 5

    Hence the answer is option (A).

Answer(A) 90∘\displaystyle 90^\circ90∘

Watch out Picking 0∘0^\circ0∘ (option D) by confusing cos⁡γ=0\cos\gamma = 0cosγ=0 with γ=0\gamma = 0γ=0.

    a⃗=i^−j^  ⇒  (1,−1,0)\vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, -1, 0)a=i^−j^​⇒(1,−1,0)a⃗=i^−j^  ⇒  (1,−1,0)\displaystyle \vec{a} = \hat{i} - \hat{j} \;\Rightarrow\; (1, -1, 0)a=i^−j^​⇒(1,−1,0)

    A parallel line has the same direction vector.

    b⃗=2i^−j^+0k^  ⇒  DRs 2,−1,0\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 0\hat{k} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{DRs } 2, -1, 0b=2i^−j^​+0k^⇒DRs 2,−1,0b⃗=2i^−j^+0k^  ⇒  DRs 2,−1,0\displaystyle \vec{b} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 0\hat{k} \;\Rightarrow\; \text{DRs } 2, -1, 0b=2i^−j^​+0k^⇒DRs 2,−1,0

    Write the Cartesian form.

    A zero denominator only means zzz stays 000 on the line.

Answer(B) x−12=y+1−1=z0\displaystyle \dfrac{x-1}{2} = \dfrac{y+1}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{0}2x−1​=−1y+1​=0z​

    x2=y−12=z−3  ⇒  2,−12,−3\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y}{-12} = \dfrac{z}{-3} \;\Rightarrow\; 2, -12, -32x​=−12y​=−3z​⇒2,−12,−3x2=y−12=z−3  ⇒  2,−12,−3\displaystyle \dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y}{-12} = \dfrac{z}{-3} \;\Rightarrow\; 2, -12, -32x​=−12y​=−3z​⇒2,−12,−3

    3(2)+2(−12)+(−6)(−3)=6−24+18=03(2) + 2(-12) + (-6)(-3) = 6 - 24 + 18 = 03(2)+2(−12)+(−6)(−3)=6−24+18=03(2)+2(−12)+(−6)(−3)=6−24+18=0\displaystyle 3(2) + 2(-12) + (-6)(-3) = 6 - 24 + 18 = 03(2)+2(−12)+(−6)(−3)=6−24+18=0

Assertion (A): If a line makes angles α,β,γ\alpha, \beta, \gammaα,β,γ with the positive directions of the coordinate axes, then sin⁡2α+sin⁡2β+sin⁡2γ=2\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma = 2sin2α+sin2β+sin2γ=2. Reason (R): The sum of squares of the direction cosines of a line is 111.

Tap the option you think is right.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Direction cosines l=cos⁡αl = \cos\alphal=cosα, m=cos⁡βm = \cos\betam=cosβ, n=cos⁡γn = \cos\gamman=cosγ satisfy l2+m2+n2=1l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1l2+m2+n2=1.

  1. 1

    Check Assertion: write each sin⁡2\sin^2sin2 as 1−cos⁡21 - \cos^21−cos2.

    sin⁡2α+sin⁡2β+sin⁡2γ=3−(cos⁡2α+cos⁡2β+cos⁡2γ)\sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma = 3 - (\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma)sin2α+sin2β+sin2γ=3−(cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ)sin⁡2α+sin⁡2β+sin⁡2γ=3−(cos⁡2α+cos⁡2β+cos⁡2γ)\displaystyle \sin^2\alpha + \sin^2\beta + \sin^2\gamma = 3 - (\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma)sin2α+sin2β+sin2γ=3−(cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ)
  2. 2

    Use cos⁡2α+cos⁡2β+cos⁡2γ=1\cos^2\alpha + \cos^2\beta + \cos^2\gamma = 1cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ=1. So A is true.

    =3−1=2= 3 - 1 = 2=3−1=2
  3. 3

    Check Reason: l2+m2+n2=1l^2 + m^2 + n^2 = 1l2+m2+n2=1 is a standard result. So R is true.

  4. 4

    R is exactly the fact used to prove A, so R explains A.

    1
  5. 5

    Hence the answer is option (A).

Answer(A) Both true; R is the correct explanation of A.

Find the shortest distance between the lines l1l_1l1​ and l2l_2l2​ whose vector equations are r⃗=(−i^−j^−k^)+λ(7i^−6j^+k^)\vec{r} = (-\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(7\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + \hat{k})r=(−i^−j^​−k^)+λ(7i^−6j^​+k^) and r⃗=(3i^+5j^+7k^)+μ(i^−2j^+k^)\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})r=(3i^+5j^​+7k^)+μ(i^−2j^​+k^), where λ\lambdaλ and μ\muμ are parameters.

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.
